title: Python: M1, an imported module-level instance (a single binding to a constructor) resolves across the import (DEC-303 (a22) item 3)
description: DEC-303 (a22) item 3, group M1, verbatim: 'M1, imported module-level instance: admitted as the (a2) 3 single binding to a constructor, carried across the import, with item 2s same-module global proviso.' Governing line (a22) item 2: a target is admitted when EVERY binding of the name can be enumerated from the text of its scope; for a module-level name, writes through global in the same module count; a write from outside the module (m.X = ...) is the accepted blind spot. First in the DEC-303 (a23) build order after K1 and LIT (M1, R4, ALIAS, TS, Q1, then (a25), NB-b, step 5) that releases the (a36) hold on the fresh blind sample. Reuse the GCLI-108 and GCLI-109 findings: one binding enumeration (enumerableBindings) with global and nonlocal provisos; enumerate every way the module-level name can get a second binding (rebind, augmented, for, with-as, except-as, walrus, comprehension target, match capture, import, def, class, del, global write from a function, a class body between use and binding, an annotated binding, a module-level star import) and give each its own refused fixture with a positive twin. Import forms to cover: from m import inst, import m then m.inst.method(), aliases, and the A4 module-file-only limit (a package __init__ stays unresolved).

acceptanceCriteria.text: an instance bound exactly once at module level of a module file to a constructor call of one in-repo class, imported by from m import inst (alias allowed), resolves a method call on it to that class method, with red-before fixtures and positive and negative twins; the m.inst module-attribute form is not covered (question to opum-doc)

any second binding in the defining module (every form in the task description), a global write from a function in that module, an import of the name from a package __init__, or a constructor that is not a single known in-repo class leaves the call unresolved, each with its own refused fixture
each rule has a mutation check that goes red, and a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with any in-repo edge it creates or removes named

implementationNotes: Built (DEC-303 (a22) item 3, M1). PROBE: before the change an imported module-level instance (from m import inst; inst.run()) was receiver-needs-inference. BUILT in src/python/calls.ts: importedInstanceClass, called from resolveAttributeCall after the 6d known-class step, one segment only. The importing name must have exactly ONE binding (enumerableBindings: a rebind, a second import of the same name, a global or nonlocal write, a for or with-as or def or any other binding, or a module-level star import in the importing module refuses), that binding a resolved from or relative import with no condition, no multiply-bound reason, a module FILE target (a package __init__ stays unresolved, A4; a from-import of a submodule is the module, not an instance). In the DEFINING module the name must have exactly one binding in module scope (global writes from functions are already on it by applyScopeRedirects), no module-level star import (starMayBind), a plain UNANNOTATED assign whose right-hand side is a call whose callee, resolved FROM the defining module, is one in-repo class passing instanceClassOf (ok MRO, no __new__, no metaclass, no opaque base, no replacing decorator: stricter than the 6d local case on purpose). Re-export hops are whatever S3 already resolves (the import target is the defining file); a rebind in the re-exporting module or an aliased re-export is refused by S3, fixtured. m.inst (module attribute access) is NOT built: the ruling text covers only the from-import carry; question put to the leader and opum-doc. modules.ts was not touched. MUTATION CHECKS (scratch python driver, replace-text mutants, each run with bun test test/python-calls.test.ts -t M1): importer count, importer enumeration (enumerableBindings to lookupBindings), reason (multiply-bound), condition, __init__ check, submodule check, star check, defining-module count, annotation check, instanceClassOf, callee scope: all 11 RED.
